professional_bio:
I am a doctoral researcher at the UCL Energy Institute and a strategic leader at the intersection of energy, economics and policy. My research addresses the "Energy Trilemma" within Nigeria’s evolving state-level markets, utilising Linear Programming and Game Theory to engineer market structures that balance energy security, consumer affordability, and rapid green energy adoption.

My perspective is uniquely shaped by a blend of technical academic rigor and "on-the-ground" commercial experience in both the UK and Nigerian power sectors. Having served as a PPA Executive at Renewable Exchange in the UK, where I brokered over 100 renewable energy contracts, I developed a deep mastery of commodity price movements and hedging strategies. Currently, as the Head of Strategy and Finance at Solarflares Energy, I lead the financial structuring of renewable-powered EV infrastructure in Lagos, bridging the gap between technical feasibility and investor appetite.

My PhD focus is on shifting market dynamics away from inefficient "Prisoner’s Dilemma" scenarios toward Nash Equilibria where private profit and social welfare align. I am committed to building the mathematical and financial frameworks necessary to turn Nigeria into a global model for decentralised, efficient, and renewable-driven power.
